description: Negative-benchmark fixture: Diesel-chain co-hallucination class. Reproduces the assetman pattern where external trait methods (.get_result/.load/.execute) chained on a query builder share bare names with internal methods on AssetRepo + IntrospectService. Any edge from `entry` to an internal *.get_result/*.load/*.execute is a phantom by construction.

forbidden_emitted_calls.reason: Diesel RunQueryDsl::get_result is an external trait method; chained on users.filter(...).get_result(). MUST NOT bind to AssetRepo.get_result or IntrospectService.get_result via bare-name suffix-match or fuzzy fallback.
Diesel RunQueryDsl::load is an external trait method; chained on users.filter(...).load(). MUST NOT bind to AssetRepo.load.

Regression-prevention (FIXED by Phase 3d). Diesel RunQueryDsl::execute is an external trait method; chained on users.execute(). The previous resolver bound `users.execute(conn)` to AssetRepo.execute via cross-package-heuristic because `users` was brought into scope by a function-scoped `use schema::users::dsl::users;` that parse_rust_imports didn't see (it walks file scope only). Phase 3d adds use_declaration handling in handle_type_assigns: function-scoped uses now emit a TypeAssign so `users` has a known receiver type (the local Struct). Tier 2's existing dropAll path drops bindings on `users.execute()` because no AssetRepo Method has parent matching.

Diesel QueryDsl::filter is an external trait method on the query builder. No internal `filter` method exists in this fixture; the pattern is here to catch future shadow targets if the resolver loosens.

notes:
Project name resolves to `c-Users-user-Documents-GitHub-code-graph-bench-accuracy-synthetic-rust-diesel-negative` per pipeline.ProjectNameFromPath (verified via bench/accuracy/check_go_minimal_resolver_rule.py:project_for_path). QN format follows the FLATTENED-mod convention from rust-minimal/ground_truth.json: impl scope IS included (AssetRepo.get_result), inline mod scope IS NOT (helper, not main.helper for fn directly under file scope). Schema reference: bench/accuracy/synthetic/_schema.md. Authored 2026-05-02 per roundtable Recommendation #1.

EMPIRICAL FINDINGS DISCOVERED VIA THIS FIXTURE (2026-05-02):
  1. cross-package-heuristic emits `entry -> AssetRepo.execute` even though `entry` only calls `users.execute(conn)` (Diesel chain). Real co-hallucination, exactly as the roundtable flagged.
  2. Bare-name resolution conflates same-named methods across receiver types. `controls()` calls both `repo.get_result()` and `service.get_result()`; only the first emits (to AssetRepo.get_result). The IntrospectService.get_result edge is silently absorbed. This is a separate but related class — same `cross-package-heuristic` rule, no receiver-type discrimination.
  3. Turbofish-suffixed chain calls (`.get_result::<User>(conn)`) don't appear to emit method-call edges. The `entry -> *.get_result` and `entry -> *.load` phantoms are absent because of the turbofish form, not because the resolver is correct. The simple form `.execute(conn)` does emit the phantom. Investigate as separate finding.
  4. Constructor calls (`AssetRepo::new()`, `IntrospectService::new()`) don't emit CALLS edges. Different code path than instance method calls. Note for receiver-type tracking work.

The positive_internal_calls list reflects what code-graph emits TODAY (2026-05-02), not what an ideal resolver would emit. When the bare-name conflation bug is fixed, expect IntrospectService.get_result and the constructor edges to be added to this list.
